meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Panama (Republic of Panama) - unitary national jurisdiction, no sub-state tax distinction
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid Civil Law: Romano-Germanic civil code foundation overlaid with common-law-influenced corporate, trust and foundation statutes; unitary national commercial registry system
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama-United States Bilateral Investment Treaty (entered into force 1991)
Panama-United Kingdom Bilateral Investment Treaty (in force)
Panama-United States Trade Promotion Agreement (in force 2012)
Panama-South Korea Double Taxation Agreement (in force)
Panama-Netherlands Double Taxation Agreement (signed and ratified process completed)
WTO membership (1997) with GATS financial-services commitments

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: PIF: Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Regimen de Fundaciones de Interes Privado), as amended by Ley No. 41 de 2000 and Ley No. 36 de 2013. AML/CFT: Ley No. 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 on prevention of money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing, its implementing Decreto Ejecutivo No. 363 de 12 de septiembre de 2017 (Beneficial Ownership Register), and binding rulings of the Superintendencia de Sujetos No Financieros (SSNF). Beneficial-ownership declarations are filed through the confidential register administered by the Direccion General de Ingresos (DGI/MEF); resident agents are regulated DPMS subjects under Law 23/2015. Apostilles: Hague Convention of 5 October 1961 approved by Ley No. 34 de 30 de octubre de 2017, in force for Panama since 8 January 2018.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of the passport of the natural-person founder, or certificate of incorporation and directors register of a corporate founder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Civil registry, competent notary, or corporate registry of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the issuing state is an Apostille member; consular legalization for non-member states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized banker's reference letter and sworn declaration of source of funds of the founder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial bank and notary public in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or active status certificate of any corporate founder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or official business registry of the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized proof of residential or registered address of the founder (utility bill or bank statement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or financial institution in the country of origin, with notarization
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; domestic notarization accepted where apostille is not applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Special power of attorney granted to the Panamanian resident agent for incorporation filings, in Spanish or accompanied by certified Spanish translation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the executing jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory customer due diligence on the founder, foundation council members, protector, beneficiaries and authorized representatives prior to incorporation. Continuous screening against: (i) UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists; (ii) OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions lists; (iii) EU consolidated financial sanctions lists; and (iv) Panamanian UAF and Public Ministry domestic lists. Politically Exposed Persons, including domestic PEPs, family members and close associates, are subject to enhanced due diligence per Law 23/2015 and SSNF directives. Suspicious findings are documented in the AML file and reported to the Unidad de Analisis Financiero (UAF) as required. Beneficial owners holding 25% or more of the foundation patrimony or exercising ultimate control are identified, verified and recorded in the DGI/SSNF government-only register; client records are retained by the resident agent for at least five years after termination of the relationship. The fintech software scope (ISIC 6201) and non-licensed status do not eliminate the PIF-level AML obligations of the resident agent.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Publico de Panama - Plataforma de Servicios en Linea, module 'Reserva de Nombre' (https://www.registropublico.gob.pa), operated by the Direccion General del Registro Publico; in-person alternative at the DIP (Direccion de Informacion) counter, Registro Publico headquarters, Panama City
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Applications must be drafted in Spanish. The proposed name must use Latin script and, where the brand is foreign, be transliterated into Spanish phonetics; diacritics and special characters not native to Spanish are normalized. Under Article 4 of Law 25 of 1995, the registrable name must incorporate the suffix 'Fundacion de Interes Privado' or an equivalent expression clearly indicating a private foundation, combined with the distinctive denomination. The name must not be identical or phonetically or orally similar to any name already reserved or registered, and must not misrepresent the entity as a corporation, bank, insurer, securities firm, or state body.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banco; Banca; Bank (requires prior non-opposition of the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panama - SBP)
Seguros; Reaseguros; Aseguradora (requires prior approval of the Superintendencia de Seguros y Reaseguros - SSN)
Fondo de Inversion; Valores; Bolsa; Casa de Bolsa; Corredor de Valores; Mercado de Valores (requires prior approval of the Superintendencia del Mercado de Valores - SMV)
Financiera; Credito; Prestamo; Ahorro; Tarjeta de Credito; Caja de Ahorros (highly restricted financial terms; SBP/SSNF caution required)
Gobierno; Nacional; Ministerio; Estatal; Oficial; Publico (state-affiliated terms requiring express ministerial authorization)
Cruz Roja; Media Luna Roja; Fundacion de Beneficencia; Fundacion de Interes Publico (public-benefit or charitable designations incompatible with the private interest foundation regime)
S.A.; Sociedad Anonima; Corp.; Inc.; LLC (corporate forms incompatible with a Private Interest Foundation)
Panama; Internacional; Mundial (restricted where confusing or suggestive of official sponsorship)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations Act), as amended; core provisions: arts. 4 (legal capacity), 6 (mandatory charter content), 8 (initial endowment of B/.10,000), 9 (resident agent), and 13-20 (Foundation Council, officers, and protective provisions).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Dirección General de Registro, Sección de Personas Jurídicas (Public Registry of Panama, Legal Entities Section)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública No. ____ — Foundation Charter (Fundación de Interés Privado), recorded under a 'Ficha' in the Registered Foundations Portfolio
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Initial endowment of at least USD 10,000 (Art. 8, Ley 25 de 1995) must be declared in the charter and attributed to the foundation's patrimony; no escrow deposit or share-capital payment is required since a PIF issues no shares — proof of the endowment is the founder's declaration in the public deed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Foundation acknowledges receipt of the initial endowment of USD 10,000 and accepts the assets contributed by the Founder as the Foundation's capital, free of any further contribution obligations; RESOLVED, that the registered office is fixed at the office of the Resident Agent, and the licensed agent is appointed and retained under Law 25 of 1995, as amended; RESOLVED, that the Foundation Council is constituted and the undersigned are elected as Council members; the President, Secretary and Treasurer are authorized to administer the Foundation's assets, execute contracts and appoint delegates to operate the financial portfolio tracking software; RESOLVED, that this resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engagement of Licensed Panamanian Resident Agent and Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección de Personas Jurídicas (approved resident-agent panel); Superintendencia de Sujetos No Financieros (AML oversight)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select and engage an attorney or licensed corporate services firm; execute the resident-agent retainer designating the agent's office as the statutory registered office; assemble the KYC file of the founder and proposed Foundation Council members before drafting the charter.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of founder and intended council members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the chosen agent declines or loses licensing, re-engage an alternate entity on the Registry's approved list; pre-formation changes of agent require no Registry filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Review and Notarization of Foundation Charter (Escritura Pública)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notario Público del Primer Circuito de Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The attorney finalizes the Spanish-language charter containing the foundation name, registered office, purpose (ISIC 6201 financial portfolio-tracking software), USD 10,000 endowment, beneficiary clauses and Foundation Council provisions under arts. 6-8 of Ley 25. The founder appears before the notary personally or by apostilled power of attorney; the notary authenticates the deed.
required_dossiers: Charter draft approved by the resident agent
Valid passport or apostilled power of attorney
Acceptance letters of initial Council members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct notarial certifications or charter recitals and re-execute before the same notary; if a name conflict is flagged by the Registry, obtain name clearance before re-signing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission and Registration with the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección de Personas Jurídicas
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the certified first notarial copy of the Escritura Pública together with proof of payment of the registration fee. The Registry assigns the 'Ficha' number and inscribes the foundation, typically within 15 working days; after inscription, a certification of legal existence is ordered.
required_dossiers: First notarial copy of the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a 'nota de observación' or defect notice, cure within the peremptory term (generally 20 working days); file a 'recurso de reconsideración' or resubmit the corrected deed; re-pay inscription fees if the term lapses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certification of Legal Existence and Registry Excerpts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Dirección de Certificaciones
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Request the 'Certificado de Existencia' and, for banking and payment-rail onboarding, certified copies of the inscribed charter and Council appointments.
required_dossiers: Written request signed by the resident agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Use the agent's expedited certification channel; if the certificate reflects stale Council data, file a charter amendment (modificación) before reordering the certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Panama Tax Registration — RUC and Flat Annual Company Tax Setup (DGI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After inscription, file the RUC registration (Form 40-1) through the DGI online portal (SERTRACEN/Panadata). The Foundation receives a RUC/NIT and is enrolled for the flat annual foundation tax of USD 300 under Ley 25; foreign-source software revenue remains outside Panama's territorial income tax base.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the registered Foundation Charter
Council members' identification and appointing resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI queries the address or Council details, resubmit the clean Registry certification; rectify via amended Form 40-1; escalate to the DGI Jefatura de Contribuyentes if the RUC is not assigned within 10 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening, Payment-Rails Activation and Municipal Compliance Check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (licensed banks); Alcaldía de Panamá (optional Aviso de Operación); Stripe and Apple IAP as payment processors
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the Foundation's corporate bank account and register the Foundation as the merchant entity for Stripe (global account) and Apple IAP under Council authorization. If a physical Panama office is maintained, file the municipal Aviso de Operación; otherwise confirm in writing that no local industrial or operational permit applies to ISIC 6201 software activity.
required_dossiers: App description, store URLs and source-of-funds statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines, supplement the AML file with reference letters or appoint an external fund administrator; if Stripe flags the PIF, resubmit with the tax classification certificate and Council signing authority, or register the merchant under a supported payments jurisdiction after confirming platform availability.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — ISIC 6201 (software and financial portfolio-tracking platform) requires no industrial license from the Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI). A municipal Aviso de Operación is filed with the Alcaldía de Panamá only if the Foundation maintains a physical office in Panama.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sectoral license required: software/cloud service is a non-regulated activity; the PIF itself is governed solely by Ley 25 de 1995 and the AML rules applicable to resident agents.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) — Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Category III — no EIA dossier required: the platform is a cloud software service with no construction, no industrial installation and no effluent discharge; activity is equivalent to administrative office/data-processing use.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharge or VOC thresholds apply. For any Panamanian office: comply with MiAMBIENTE Resolution AG-0358-2014 on acoustic levels and Law 38 de 2019 on segregated waste; ICT and e-waste must be delivered to an authorized recycler; if a backup generator is installed, comply with the emission limits adopted by MiAMBIENTE for stationary engines.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá fire-safety inspection and operating certificate for office premises; Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL) occupational health and safety clearance under Resolution No. 7 de 2015; structural load certification by a licensed engineer is required only for tenant improvements or server-room reinforcement.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) - General Directorate of Revenue, Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Republic of Panama; taxpayer portal: SIF (Sistema de Información Fiscal), https://sif.mef.gob.pa; official DGI website: https://www.dgi.gob.pa.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: (1) Register the Private Interest Foundation (PIF) constitutive act and Foundation Council with the Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry) and obtain the Ficha / certificate of legal existence. (2) Appoint a resident agent and, if the foundation becomes operational, a Panamanian licensed attorney (abogado idóneo). (3) Apply for the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente, the statutory TIN) through DGI/SIF before commencing any Panamanian-source activity, submitting: apostilled foundation deed, Registry excerpt (Ficha), notarized power of attorney, proof of local domicile and resident agent, and, for a foreign legal entity, the parent's certificate of good standing; foreign entities must also file the Aviso de Operación with the local Alcaldía when a Panamanian commercial establishment exists. (4) Obtain the DGI secure digital certificate (firma electrónica / sello de seguridad) enabling SIF e-filing and e-invoicing. (5) Register in the DGI exporter file (Registro de Exportadores de Servicios) to preserve 0% ITBMS on cross-border subscriptions. A purely passive PIF that earns only foreign-source income is not legally required to hold a RUC, but voluntary registration is advisable to monetize input VAT credits.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope - Under Law 25/1995, the PIF is a distinct legal person whose foreign-source and passive wealth-administration income, assets, transfers, and capital gains are not taxable in Panama (territorial tax system); if the PIF carries on commercial activity with Panamanian source, entity-level tax applies at standard corporate ISR rates (25%, with the Law 254/2023 progressive surcharges on profits exceeding B/.1.5 million) plus ITBMS at 7%. No pass-through of tax attributes to founders or beneficiaries exists.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama has no US-style check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch passthrough election. Statutory elections relevant to the PIF: (i) small-taxpayer regime election (Régimen de Pequeño Contribuyente - RPC; 2% of gross receipts in lieu of ISR and ITBMS, available where annual gross revenue does not exceed B/.200,000); (ii) election to remain an ordinary ITBMS registrant to recover input VAT on export costs; (iii) election to issue e-invoices through a certified third-party agent (agente facturador) versus direct SIF API integration; (iv) PIF charter elections allocating income and wealth to named beneficiaries abroad, which are not Panamanian source and therefore outside Panamanian withholding; and (v) transfer-pricing documentation elections for cross-border related-party transactions under Law 254/2023.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) - Panamanian VAT; Código Fiscal Articles 1057 et seq., Ley 34/2004, Decree 42/2006, as amended by Ley 254/2023
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general de-minimis threshold - ITBMS registration is triggered by the mere carrying-on of taxable transfers of goods or services in Panama. Optional simplified small-taxpayer regime (RPC) applies to annual gross revenue up to B/.200,000 (threshold raised from B/.36,000 by Law 254/2023). Non-resident digital platforms (e.g., foreign app stores) must register for digital-services ITBMS where consumers are Panamanian residents. A PIF with only foreign subscription customers has no ITBMS nexus in Panama.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing (Facturación Electrónica en Línea - FEL) administered through the DGI SIF platform under DGI Resolution 201-4458/2023, with a phased rollout: taxpayers with annual gross revenue above B/.5 million (FY2022), B/.250,000-B/.5 million (FY2023), and all remaining taxpayers on the 2024-2025 DGI calendar. Statutory model: real-time fiscal clearance via SIF REST/SOAP web services; taxpayer software or a certified agente facturador submits UBL 2.1 XML invoices to DGI and receives an immediate Aceptada/Rechazada authorization; printed invoice must carry a QR verification code and DGI digital stamp (sello electrónico). Offline contingency billing is limited to 48 hours using a 'C' prefix. Monthly electronic declaration of sales and purchases ledgers (Libro de Ventas / Libro de Compras) and e-filing of the ITBMS return are mandatory.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The supply is charged at 0% ITBMS with entitlement to input VAT refund where: (a) goods are physically exported from Panama under a customs export declaration; or (b) services, including SaaS financial-portfolio-tracking subscriptions sold via Stripe and Apple IAP, meet all four conditions: (i) the recipient is a non-resident, (ii) the benefit is effectively used or consumed entirely outside Panama, (iii) the service is not connected to Panamanian real property, and (iv) the consideration is paid from abroad in foreign currency. For the fintech application, DGI accepts geo-located digital evidence (customer billing country, IP address logs, platform subscription records, and the signed service agreement) to evidence offshore consumption. Sales to Panamanian resident users remain taxable at 7% ITBMS.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única Aduanera - DUA) - for physical goods exports only
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill evidencing physical export movement (consolidated logistics file)
Commercial invoice (FACTURA) stating 'ITBMS 0% - Exportación de Bienes/Servicios'
Signed service agreement or platform terms identifying the foreign recipient and the place of benefit
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank certificate) proving foreign-currency proceeds credited to a Panamanian bank account
Customer non-residency evidence (billing address, foreign tax identification, passport/apostilled certificate, or geo-IP platform report)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export refund claims (saldo a favor) are automatically selected for DGI documentary verification before payment. If the substantiation bundle is incomplete or inconsistent, DGI re-characterizes the supply as domestic: collection of omitted ITBMS at 7%, monthly late-payment interest of 1% (12% annual), surcharge fines of 25%-200% of the omitted tax (Law 254/2023), and revocation of exporter refund status. Deliberate or false export zero-rating constitutes criminal tax fraud (defraudación tributaria), punishable by fines up to B/.250,000 and imprisonment for up to 10 years in aggravated cases, with joint and several liability of Foundation Council members and potential seizure of the PIF's assets. Assessments may be reopened within the statutory prescription period (generally 5 years, extended in cases of non-filing).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama operates under full dollarization and has no traditional central bank. The Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (Superintendency of Banks of Panama, SBP), established under Legislative Decree No. 2 of 2008, is the sole banking and AML/CFT supervisor. Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as fiscal agent of the State, while the Ministry of Economy and Finance handles public-debt and liquidity policy in coordination with the international banking system. There is no dedicated foreign-exchange administration, no exchange-control agency, and no central-bank approval requirement for treasury operations; monetary policy is effectively delegated to the United States Federal Reserve through the dollarized currency regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The United States Dollar is full legal tender in Panama; the Panamanian Balboa (PAB) circulates only as token coinage at a fixed 1:1 parity and is not an independent monetary unit. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are fully convertible with zero statutory restrictions, no surrender obligations, no central-bank prior-approval, and no settlement delays. Profit remittance hurdles are minimal: Panama applies a territorial income-tax model, so foreign-source revenue of non-resident-owned Private Interest Foundations is not subject to Panamanian corporate income tax; only Panamanian-source income is taxable. Dividends paid from Panamanian-source profits attract a 10% withholding tax, and branches remitting to foreign head offices attract a 10% remittance tax, but a pure fintech software and portfolio-tracking PIF generating revenue offshore faces no Panamanian remittance tax. No currency-conversion friction exists because the treasury operating and reporting currency is USD.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Panama imposes no statutory timeline for the repatriation of export proceeds and no mandatory conversion ratio for export or service receipts. Software subscriptions, licensing revenue, and SaaS disbursements (ISIC 6201) may be retained offshore, settled in USD, or converted into third currencies at the operator's discretion without any central-bank filing or foreign-exchange declaration.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Corporate USD Operating Account with Integrated Treasury and Dealing Desk
Operational USD Account and Merchant Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM as a collection sub-rail and LOW as a primary treasury custody layer. Panamanian law has no Electronic Money Institution (EMI) licensing category; only SBP-licensed banks may lawfully take deposits in Panama. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer, and Revolut Business may be engaged as payment-facilitation counterparts for inbound software sales and outbound vendor disbursements, but they are unregulated from a Panamanian perspective and typically subject the PIF to their own heightened AML screening. Legal constraints: (i) an EMI account does not constitute a Panamanian bank account and cannot satisfy the foundation's banking-reference requirement; (ii) all corporate identification materials, including the Foundation Charter, Certificate of Good Standing, and the final-beneficial-owner extract, must be apostilled and provided to the EMI; (iii) funds left in an EMI at year-end trigger no Panamanian tax but expose the PIF to PSP freezing risk, FX drift, and card-scheme reserve holds. Recommended architecture: use EMI rails exclusively for daily collections from Stripe and Apple IAP, with daily sweeping into an SBP-licensed USD operating account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Panamanian banks generally require a physical onboarding interview for non-resident-owned PIFs. At least one of the following must appear in person before the bank's compliance officer: a member of the Foundation Council, the Resident Agent, or an individual holding written power of attorney granted by the Council. Remote video onboarding is permitted only as a controlled alternative when the ultimate beneficial owner cannot travel, and it must be executed through the bank's secure channel with biometric verification, supplemented by notarized identity confirmation before a Panamanian consul or apostilled under the Hague Apostille Convention. Purely paperless and fully remote opening is not permitted under SBP due-diligence rules (Acuerdo 004-2017 and Law 254 of 2021), because the final-beneficial-owner register requires in-person identity confirmation of the settlor's natural-person UBO. In practice, the Resident Agent's certification of good standing and at least one physical appearance are mandatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Settlor or UBO domiciled in a higher-risk jurisdiction, having tax-related reputational exposure, or qualifying as a politically exposed person (PEP)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-wealth file: audited financial statements or certified tax returns of the settlor for at least three years, bank statements evidencing accumulation of the foundation endowment, sale and purchase deeds for real property or intellectual property, a sworn declaration of legitimate origin, and a PEP-negative due-diligence report issued by an SBP-accredited vendor within 90 days of onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discretionary beneficiary structure or protector rights creating ambiguity over beneficial ownership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foundation Charter containing a registered beneficiary schedule, Council Resolution listing all current council members and the protector with nationality and residential address, an extract of the Registro de Beneficiarios Finales under Law 254 of 2021, and an irrevocable undertaking to the bank that any change to beneficiaries, council members, or the protector will be notified within five business days.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business-model mismatch: software app (ISIC 6201) collecting revenue via Stripe and Apple IAP without a local payments license
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate and product file: platform schedule describing the wealth-analytics and portfolio-tracking service, Apple and Google app-store agreements, Stripe merchant agreement with processing-volume projections, a legal opinion confirming that the PIF does not take deposits or provide payment services because it merely receives its own commercial revenue, and the PIF's registry certificate showing no regulated-activity engagement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction velocity disproportionate to foundation capital or to stated subscription volumes
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Treasury defense file: annual budget and cash-flow forecast, subscriber and annual-recurring-revenue metrics, unit-economics dashboard, controller attestation on platform-fee settlement cycles, and a funds-flow map from Stripe and Apple IAP through the EMI sub-rails into the SBP-licensed operating account with clearing timestamps.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual source of the endowment capital, including cryptocurrency, intangible property, or intercompany loans
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Asset provenance report: chain-of-title records for contributed intellectual property, an independent appraiser's valuation report, executed loan agreements and intercompany balance confirmations, licensed-venue exchange withdrawal history and trading statements if cryptocurrency was used, and the certified public deed of the capital endowment recorded at the Registro Público.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: the settlor executes a certified capital-endowment deed, and funds flow by SWIFT MT103, or MT202 for larger interbank transfers, from the settlor's bank to the PIF's USD account at an SBP-licensed Panamanian bank. The wire instruction must include: (i) the beneficiary PIF name exactly as registered, (ii) the foundation registry number, (iii) a purpose code or field 70 statement such as 'Foundation capital contribution under Law 25 of 1995' or 'Foundation endowment funding', and (iv) a reference to the endowment resolution. For amounts up to USD 100,000, the bank typically requires only the Foundation Charter and Certificate of Good Standing; above USD 500,000 it requires a source-of-wealth questionnaire; above USD 1,000,000 it requires an independent source-of-funds audit. Inbound remittances must originate from a bank account in the settlor's own name to avoid third-party-funding rejections. No central-bank approval or foreign-investment permit is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outward payments are cleared through the Panamanian bank's USD correspondent, typically Citibank N.A., JPMorgan Chase, or The Bank of New York Mellon in New York, using SWIFT MT103 for operating disbursements such as cloud-infrastructure bills, licensing fees, subscription refunds, salaries, and vendor payments. Commercial Letters of Credit are available for infrastructure procurement and are issued via SWIFT MT700, with settlement on MT202 or MT103 over corresponding account rails. EUR-denominated disbursements settle via TARGET2 using SWIFT MT103 in EUR. Domestic clearing in Panama is fully USD-denominated through the local ACH operator and the Clave system, which process only retail USD payments; no Balboa non-cash settlement exists. Recommended treasury policy: maintain banking redundancy across two tier-1 banks, perform daily sweeping of EMI balances into the licensed account, separate the settlement account from the custody and investment account, and pre-approve MT103 batch files with dual-authorization thresholds.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Offshore deliverable FX forwards (USD/EUR and USD/GBP) executed with the Panamanian bank's treasury desk or a US prime broker under an ISDA Master Agreement
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on Latin American emerging currencies (USD/MXN, USD/BRL, USD/COP) with tier-1 global bank counterparties
Cross-currency swaps (USD/EUR interest-rate and FX basis swaps) under ISDA and CSA documentation for multi-year subscription-revenue hedging
Vanilla FX options and zero-cost collars for EUR and GBP flow protection
FX spot interbank executed through the bank's dealing desk strictly for settlement, with no speculative position-taking

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Private Interest Foundation franchise tax (Tasa Anual de Fundación de Interés Privado), comprising the official annual tax voucher and payment confirmation submitted through the resident agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF); remitted through the Registro Público de Panamá single-window official collection channel
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January – 31 March of each calendar year; payable annually in advance for the current registration year; 31 March (or the next business day if on a weekend or holiday) is the definitive no-surcharge cutoff
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: B/.350.00 if paid between 1 April and 30 June; B/.400.00 if paid after 30 June; the Registro Público will refuse certifications of existence and good standing (certificado de registro y estar al día) until the fee is settled; three consecutive unpaid years permit the DGI to begin administrative strike-off from the Public Registry, and the resident agent remains jointly liable as payer of record

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO reaffirmation (confirmación anual del Registro de Beneficiario Final) and any amendment statements reporting changes in ultimate beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Registro de Beneficiario Final (RUBF) unit, coordinated exclusively by the registered resident agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days after any change in the founder, beneficiaries, Foundation Council members, or protector; otherwise as part of the annual renewal cycle consistent with the franchise tax window of 1 January – 31 March; an unchanged RUBF file may be satisfied by the resident agent's annual reaffirmation in the renewal filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines under Law 70 of 2019 and its implementing decrees, withholding of notarial attestations and registry certifications, placement of a 'pending compliance' annotation blocking further filings, and suspension of registry services for chronic non-compliance until the RUBF file is cured

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Conditional annual corporate income tax declaration (Declaración Jurada de Impuesto sobre la Renta) reflecting territorial-source income; nil or exempt status applies where the PIF derives no Panamanian-source revenue
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance, via the official DGI e-filing platform (e-Tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 March following the close of the calendar fiscal year for a 31 December year-end; a three-month anniversary rule applies for any non-calendar fiscal year approved by the DGI
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Interest accrues at 1% per month on unpaid Panamanian-source income tax, a non-filing surcharge of up to 10% of the assessed tax applies, ex-officio assessment may be issued, and continued non-response permits the DGI to pursue enforced collection or strike-off proceedings

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Law 25 private interest foundations are not audited by default and their books are private; an independent audit by a Panamanian licensed CPA becomes mandatory when (i) gross annual income from Panamanian territorial sources reaches USD 250,000 under DGI 'estados financieros dictaminados' practice, (ii) the foundation's charter, regulations, or a protector direction expressly requires audited accounts, or (iii) a counterparty or regulatory regime (e.g., banking credit, insurance, securities) imposes an audit; a PIF engaged purely in passive cross-border fintech portfolio tracking generally remains below all trigger thresholds
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS), including IFRS for SMEs, as adopted by Panama's Comisión de Normas de Contabilidad; Panama does not maintain a separate authoritative local GAAP for private interest foundations

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial taxation: foreign-source active and passive income is exempt from Panamanian corporate income tax; a Private Interest Foundation (PIF) holding foreign portfolio assets typically incurs only the USD 400 annual flat government tax, not ISR on such foreign income. Preferential SME rates apply to taxpayers with gross taxable income below B/. 200,000 per annum, and special regimes (e.g., Panama Pacifico, Multinational Headquarters 'SEM') may grant reduced effective rates for qualifying licensed activities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 120 (Informe de Renta Anual) filed electronically through the DGI e-Tax portal (T@-P-30). Line/box captions follow the current official Form 120 worksheet; DGI may revise box numbering on each annual form release. A PIF without Panamanian-source income is generally not required to file Form 120 but must pay the annual USD 400 flat tax via the Treasury/Public Registry payment channels.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after fiscal year-end; for calendar-year taxpayers, no later than March 31 of the following year. Individuals under certain regimes may use the extended calendar set by DGI, but corporate filers must observe the three-month rule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue derived from Panamanian-source commercial, industrial, and financial activities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter 0 if all revenue is foreign-source and no Panamanian-source income exists; attach an explanatory schedule of foreign-source revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of sales and direct costs attributable to Panamanian-source revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter 0 where no Panamanian-source revenue exists; if mixed-source, allocate costs only against Panamanian-source revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating expenses, including administrative and selling expenses, subject to expense substantiation and transfer pricing adjustment disclosure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses incurred for the production of Panamanian-source income are deductible; foreign-head-office allocations must be supported by contemporaneous documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income before loss carryforward: Box 1 minus Box 3 minus Box 5 plus non-deductible add-backs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute strictly on Panamanian-source taxable items; do not offset foreign-source losses against Panamanian-source gains.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net operating loss (NOL) carryforward deduction, limited to losses sustained within the prior five fiscal years as recognized by DGI.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-source losses are not eligible; only losses arising from Panamanian-source activity and previously reported to DGI may be claimed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income before credits: taxable base after NOL and exemptions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the standard 25% rate or applicable SME preferential rate only to Panamanian-source taxable base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross corporate income tax at statutory rate (25%).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute at 25%; SME taxpayers meeting turnover thresholds apply the preferential rate per DGI instructions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits: quarterly advance payments (Caja Única), tax withholdings, foreign tax credits on Panamanian-source income, and other statutory credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits are unavailable for exempt foreign-source income; claim only Panamanian-source withholding and advance payment credits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax payable or refund balance after credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where all income is foreign-source and no Panamanian withholding was applied, enter 0 and confirm the PIF annual flat tax has been paid.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing surcharge of 10% of the tax due for the first month of delay plus 2% per month or fraction thereof, capped at 30% of the tax due; moratory interest accrues at the statutory monthly rate; administrative fines for non-filing range from B/. 50 to B/. 500. If the understated tax exceeds B/. 300,000, criminal tax fraud liability may attach separately.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends or profit distributions paid out of profits that have been subject to corporate income tax; 20% withholding on dividends and deemed distributions paid out of untaxed or non-taxed profits, including Panamanian-source earnings not previously assessed.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a Double Taxation Agreement (DTA) reduction, the foreign recipient must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its home tax authority, deliver the TRC and a beneficial ownership declaration to the Panamanian withholding agent before payment, and complete the DGI prescribed application (Form 226 or successor) for reduced withholding; the withholding agent submits the TRC package to DGI and applies the treaty rate only upon acknowledgment, retaining all records for at least five years. Active Panamanian DTAs include those with Mexico, Singapore, South Korea, the United Arab Emirates, and Barbados; the specific dividend rate depends on the treaty's threshold ownership conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory 15% withholding on royalties and technical fees paid to non-residents for the use of intellectual property or services exploited in Panama; statutory 15% withholding on interest paid to non-resident creditors, with an exemption for interest paid to recognized foreign banks and international financial institutions not engaged in Panamanian business. Treaty rates may reduce royalty and interest withholding to 5-10% depending on the applicable DTA and beneficial ownership.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File must be prepared and filed when annual consolidated gross revenue exceeds B/. 1,500,000 (USD equivalent). Master File is required when the multinational group's consolidated annual revenue exceeds B/. 75,000,000. Country-by-Country Report (CbCR) is required when the group's annual consolidated revenue exceeds B/. 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama has adopted Economic Substance Requirements (ESR) under Law 254 of 2021 applying to entities tax-resident in Panama engaged in relevant activities such as financing, leasing, holding of shares/securities, distribution, and service provision. A PIF engaged in passive foreign portfolio tracking for non-resident beneficiaries, with management and control exercised outside Panama, generally falls outside the scope of ESR. If management, staff, or revenue-generating activities are relocated to Panama, the entity must demonstrate adequate physical premises, a proportionate number of employees, and substantial expenditures in Panama. The general anti-avoidance rule established by Law 76 of 2019 permits DGI to disregard structures lacking economic substance, reallocate income to the real beneficial owner, and disallow treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully omitting Panamanian-source revenue, filing materially false Form 120 returns, manufacturing false deductions, or disguising taxable Panamanian-source income as exempt foreign-source income in the PIF's accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Surcharge of up to 30% of the evaded tax, moratory interest, administrative fines of B/. 50 to B/. 500 per infraction, and criminal penalties of 2 to 5 years' imprisonment when the evaded tax exceeds B/. 300,000; aggravated circumstances may extend the term.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who sign false declarations or approve fraudulent filings are jointly liable for the evaded tax and civil restitution; criminal prosecution may result in imprisonment, travel bans, and disqualification from serving as directors of any Panamanian legal entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a PIF with no real economic activity, no employees, and no premises to divert or conceal the Panamanian-source business income of the beneficial owner, or to shield the identity of the ultimate beneficial owner from the Panamanian Beneficial Ownership Registry.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI may disregard the legal form, reattribute income to the beneficial owner, deny treaty relief, impose a fine of one to two times the reassessed tax, and refer the matter for criminal tax fraud prosecution; failure to report ultimate beneficial owner data to the registry carries fines up to B/. 1,000,000 per violation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who maintain a dormant or shell PIF without substance while facilitating tax avoidance face personal civil liability for restitution of the underpaid tax; prosecutorial measures may include asset freezes, travel bans, and imprisonment for complicity in tax fraud or money laundering.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting third-party funds or executing payment-rail transactions (Stripe, Apple IAP) through the PIF without customer due diligence, beneficial owner identification, transaction monitoring, or suspicious activity reporting as required by Law 23 of 2015 and DGI Supervision regulations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines scaling from B/. 10,000 to B/. 1,000,000 per violation, forced closure of the fintech platform payment accounts, asset forfeiture of funds linked to suspicious transactions, and criminal prosecution of responsible officers with imprisonment of up to 5 years for money laundering complicity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers are individually liable for AML failures; penalties include civil fines, disqualification from financial activities, travel restrictions, and criminal imprisonment where the platform knowingly processes proceeds of unlawful activity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Improper Distributions and Corporate Veil Piercing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Approving distributions, dividends, or foundation benefits without verifying the existence of legally distributable profits, or making distributions from funds that are demonstrably the beneficial owner's undeclared Panamanian-source income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil restitution of the full unlawful distribution plus interest, disallowance of deductions in the PIF's account, and a penalty of up to 30% of the improperly distributed amount; criminal liability arises if the distribution is part of a tax evasion scheme.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Panamanian courts may pierce the PIF's juridical veil where the foundation is used fraudulently or abusively; directors face joint and several liability for the corporation's tax obligations, civil damages, travel bans, attachment of personal assets, and imprisonment of 2 to 5 years where fraud is proven.
